💊 Supplements🥗 Food Log

Food Log

Daily meals with estimated nutrition, newest first.

17days logged
60meals and snacks
Estimates only. Values come from USDA FoodData Central, scaled to portions you gave or to stated assumptions, and cover only the meals logged (breakfast is not normally eaten, so none is expected; unlogged snacks are not counted). Calcium shown is the amount eaten, not the amount absorbed (for example, spinach calcium is poorly absorbed). Each day shows food, supplements and combined separately. Supplement amounts are label values times the schedule on the Supplements page. Every-other-day items (liver, glucosamine, collagen) are averaged at half a dose per day because their start day is not logged; iodine and B12 count only Mon/Wed/Fri, vitamin D3+K2 only Mon-Fri. Collagen calories are not on the label, so they are excluded. Supplement magnesium upper limit of 350 mg/day (NIH ODS) applies to supplement magnesium only, not food. Ranges reflect portion uncertainty.

Week at a glance estimates, logged meals only

One bar per day; every nutrient is its own colored layer, longest at the back. Hover, tap or Tab onto a layer to see eaten amounts, % of target, and (for calcium, potassium, magnesium and protein) an estimated absorbed vs not-absorbed split. The black tick is calories on the bottom kcal axis.

Show:
Scale:

% of each nutrient’s daily target (protein 56 g, fiber 30 g, calcium 1,000 mg, potassium 3,400 mg, magnesium 420 mg). Sodium* is against its 2,300 mg limit, so shorter is better. Dashed magenta line = 100%. Bars past the right edge are clipped.

Raw numbers on one shared axis (mg or g as logged). Small nutrients in grams look tiny, which is why % mode is the default.

Can’t see a layer? Hover, tap or Tab onto its name in the legend to bring it to the front. A small tab under a bar’s end marks a layer hidden behind another. “+” after a number means some foods had no data, so the true amount is higher. Hollow marker or hatched row = day in progress. Calories have no target; tap “Calories” in the legend to hide the tick. Estimates for a typical adult; targets are for a 54-year-old man. Tuna sandwich, curry and many portions are assumed; see each day.

        How this was estimated

        All meals logged: lunch (~1:50 PM), afternoon snack (~3:05 PM) and dinner (~9-10 PM), times approximate. Many portions are assumed. Lunch soup is store-bought with ginger and garlic added, so no salt entry. Dinner: Moshi Moshi Red Dragon roll (menu: shrimp katsu, avocado, topped with tuna, crispy onion, ponzu mayo, spicy eel sauce) built from USDA components with assumed weights for 8 pieces (piece count not on the menu); restaurant, so no added salt beyond component values, plus ~1 tbsp regular soy sauce he used (amount assumed); eel sauce uses teriyaki values and crispy onion uses fried onion ring values. Home-cooked pepper, broccoli and chicken thigh get one assumed salt entry and ~1 tsp olive oil. Totals are the sum of rows below (USDA per-100 g value x grams). "Assumed" = I chose the portion because it was not logged. Accessed 2026-10-15.

        • Fiber: no data for Short-grain white rice, cooked (sushi rice); excluded, not counted as zero.

        Notes on foods:

        • Avocado, raw: Variety not logged; USDA 'all commercial varieties' entry used. Portion (3/4 of a medium avocado) assumed.
        • Broccoli, cooked, boiled, drained, no salt: Logged as steamed; USDA boiled value used as the closest entry. Floret size assumed (~18 g each).
        • Chicken thigh, meat only, cooked, roasted: Photo shows seasoned dark-meat pieces; thigh assumed. Seasoning and any marinade or skin not counted.
        • Fairlife 2% reduced-fat ultra-filtered milk: Branded USDA entry. Label per 240 mL serving: 120 kcal, 13 g protein, 401 mg calcium, 401 mg potassium, 120 mg sodium. Magnesium (10 mg/100 mL) is from the USDA record's nutrient list, not the printed label. Values are per 100 mL; 1 mL treated as 1 g.
        • Kefir, Maple Hill organic whole-milk plain unsweetened: Per-serving label values (170 g / 2/3 cup): 120 kcal, 7 g fat, 5 g protein, 0 g fiber, 85 mg sodium, 260 mg potassium, 200 mg calcium (20% DV, per Eat This Much; the Raley's page rendering omitted the calcium line). Magnesium is not on the label; 12 mg/100 g from the Lifeway kefir entry is assumed. Converted to per 100 g. Note: a USDA branded-food record for the same product (8 oz/243 g: 180 kcal, 9 g protein, 389 mg calcium) gives higher protein/calcium per gram; the label figures were used.
        • Mayonnaise, regular: Assumed in tuna sandwich.
        • Onion, raw: Used for cooked onion too.
        • Fried onion (onion rings, breaded and fried): Fried onion rings used as a stand-in for crispy onion topping.
        • Salt, table (assumed, added to taste): salt to taste, amount assumed
        • Shrimp, breaded and fried: Breaded fried shrimp used for shrimp katsu.
        • Short-grain white rice, cooked (sushi rice): Plain cooked short-grain rice; sushi-rice vinegar seasoning (sugar, salt) not included.
        • Teriyaki sauce: Teriyaki sauce used as a stand-in for (spicy) eel sauce; USDA has no eel sauce entry.
        • Tuna, yellowfin, raw: Raw yellowfin tuna used for sushi tuna.
        • Whole Foods Market lentil soup (1 cup, 245 g): Branded USDA entry (Kettle Cuisine for Whole Foods). Blank label nutrients (potassium, magnesium) filled with USDA FNDDS (Survey) 2707462 (Soup, lentil) stand-in, accessed 2026-10-25.
        • Yogurt, plain, low fat: Brand not logged; generic USDA low-fat plain yogurt.

        How this was estimated

        All meals logged: lunch (~1 PM), afternoon snack (~3 PM), evening snack (~5:50 PM), half potato (~6:15 PM) dinner (~11 PM) and 2 oz Whole Foods lentil soup (~11:20 PM; store-bought, no added salt; no potassium/magnesium data) and 2 prunes (~11:30 PM), times approximate. Many portions are assumed. Home-cooked lunch gets one assumed salt entry (1.5 g); the potato was very mildly salted (light pinch, ~0.4 g assumed); restaurant empanadas and store-bought snacks get none. Fish is white fish of unspecified type (cod values used); the onion salad's creamy dressing is assumed to be the 2 oz kefir, not counted twice. Chocolate biscotti uses chocolate wafer cookie values; empanadas (baked, ~4 inches, ~80 g each assumed) use a generic USDA restaurant beef empanada that may include fried versions, so baked could be a bit lower in fat. Totals are the sum of rows below (USDA per-100 g value x grams). "Assumed" = I chose the portion because it was not logged. Accessed 2026-10-15.

        Data gaps:

          Notes on foods:

          • Chocolate biscotti (stand-in: chocolate wafer cookies): USDA has no biscotti entry; crisp chocolate wafer cookies used as the closest stand-in.
          • Cod, Pacific, cooked: "White fish" species unknown; cod used. USDA lists no fiber value for cod; set to 0 (animal food).
          • Beef empanada (restaurant, Latino): Generic USDA restaurant beef empanada used for GoGo Empanadas; recipes vary.
          • Fairlife 2% reduced-fat ultra-filtered milk: Branded USDA entry. Label per 240 mL serving: 120 kcal, 13 g protein, 401 mg calcium, 401 mg potassium, 120 mg sodium. Magnesium (10 mg/100 mL) is from the USDA record's nutrient list, not the printed label. Values are per 100 mL; 1 mL treated as 1 g.
          • Kale, raw: Sauteed at home; raw values used for the raw leaf weight (cooking changes weight, not nutrients much).
          • Kefir, Maple Hill organic whole-milk plain unsweetened: Per-serving label values (170 g / 2/3 cup): 120 kcal, 7 g fat, 5 g protein, 0 g fiber, 85 mg sodium, 260 mg potassium, 200 mg calcium (20% DV, per Eat This Much; the Raley's page rendering omitted the calcium line). Magnesium is not on the label; 12 mg/100 g from the Lifeway kefir entry is assumed. Converted to per 100 g. Note: a USDA branded-food record for the same product (8 oz/243 g: 180 kcal, 9 g protein, 389 mg calcium) gives higher protein/calcium per gram; the label figures were used.
          • Kombucha (Kroger brand entry): Brand not logged; this entry reports only calories and sodium/protein. Blank label nutrients (fiber, calcium, potassium, magnesium) filled with USDA SR Legacy 173227 (Beverages, tea, black, brewed, tap water; kombucha base tea, weak stand-in) stand-in.
          • Onion, raw: Used for cooked onion too.
          • Potato, baked, flesh and skin: Preparation not logged; baked with skin, no salt, assumed.
          • Salt, table (assumed, added to taste): salt to taste, amount assumed
          • SkinnyPop Original popcorn: Blank label nutrients (potassium, magnesium) filled with USDA SR Legacy 170247 (Snacks, popcorn, oil-popped, white popcorn, salt added) stand-in.
          • Whole Foods Market lentil soup (1 cup, 245 g): Branded USDA entry (Kettle Cuisine for Whole Foods). Blank label nutrients (potassium, magnesium) filled with USDA FNDDS (Survey) 2707462 (Soup, lentil) stand-in, accessed 2026-10-25.

                • Chicken thigh, meat only, cooked, roasted: Photo shows seasoned dark-meat pieces; thigh assumed. Seasoning and any marinade or skin not counted.

                • Kefir, Maple Hill organic whole-milk plain unsweetened: Per-serving label values (170 g / 2/3 cup): 120 kcal, 7 g fat, 5 g protein, 0 g fiber, 85 mg sodium, 260 mg potassium, 200 mg calcium (20% DV, per Eat This Much; the Raley's page rendering omitted the calcium line). Note: a USDA branded-food record for the same product (8 oz/243 g: 180 kcal, 9 g protein, 389 mg calcium) gives higher protein/calcium per gram; the label figures were used.
                • Kombucha (Kroger brand entry): Brand not logged; this entry reports only calories and sodium/protein.                 • Milk, 2% reduced fat: Milk type not logged; 2% assumed.
                • Salt, table (assumed, added to taste): salt to taste, amount assumed
                • Spinach, cooked, boiled, drained, no salt: Wilted dark greens (spinach-like, possibly creamed) from the photo; plain boiled spinach assumed. Any cream, oil or salt not counted.

                Data gaps:

                  Notes on foods:

                  • Cod, Pacific, cooked: "White fish" species unknown; cod used. USDA lists no fiber value for cod; set to 0 (animal food).
                  • Corn tortilla (ready-to-fry): Assumed: small corn tortilla ~27 g per flauta. Restaurant tortilla may differ.
                  • Duck meat, cooked: Assumed filling is duck (user's belief), meat only, no skin; added salt/seasoning not included.
                  • Kefir, Maple Hill organic whole-milk plain unsweetened: Per-serving label values (170 g / 2/3 cup): 120 kcal, 7 g fat, 5 g protein, 0 g fiber, 85 mg sodium, 260 mg potassium, 200 mg calcium (20% DV, per Eat This Much; the Raley's page rendering omitted the calcium line). Magnesium is not on the label; 12 mg/100 g from the Lifeway kefir entry is assumed. Converted to per 100 g. Note: a USDA branded-food record for the same product (8 oz/243 g: 180 kcal, 9 g protein, 389 mg calcium) gives higher protein/calcium per gram; the label figures were used.
                  • Kombucha (Kroger brand entry): Brand not logged; this entry reports only calories and sodium/protein. Blank label nutrients (fiber, calcium, potassium, magnesium) filled with USDA SR Legacy 173227 (Beverages, tea, black, brewed, tap water; kombucha base tea, weak stand-in) stand-in.
                  • Lentils, boiled, no salt: Home recipe/salt unknown; unsalted values used, so sodium may be higher.
                  • Melting cheese (mozzarella-type): Cheese type unknown; Oaxaca/mozzarella-type melting cheese assumed as the closest USDA entry. Could be e.g. cotija or queso fresco (different values).
                  • Milk, 2% reduced fat: Milk type not logged; 2% assumed.
                  • Salt, table (assumed, added to taste): salt to taste, amount assumed
                  • Plain Icelandic cream-skyr, strained whole-milk yogurt (The Icelandic Milk and Skyr Corp.): Brand and size of the "extra creamy" skyr are unknown; this plain whole-milk skyr label entry is assumed. Entry lacks magnesium. Blank label nutrients (magnesium) filled with USDA SR Legacy 171304 (Yogurt, Greek, plain, whole milk) stand-in.
                  • Spinach, raw: Logged as sauteed; raw values used (cooking changes weight).
                  • Vegetable oil (frying): Assumed ~5 g absorbed oil per flauta; oil type unknown, soybean used as generic vegetable oil.
